hints.title: Comparing Records Within the Same Table
hints.text: Both workers and their supervisors reside in the same employee table. How can you connect each worker record with the corresponding supervisor record using the supervisory foreign key?

hints.title: Self-Join Relationship Invariant
hints.text: A self-join treats the same table as two separate entities: one representing workers and the other representing supervisors, connected by manager identifier matching primary identifier.

hints.title: Inner Self-Join Filtering Procedure
hints.text: Perform an inner join of Employee to itself on worker manager identifier equals supervisor identifier. Filter for records where worker compensation exceeds supervisor compensation, and select the worker name.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT e.name AS Employee
FROM Employee e
JOIN Employee m ON e.managerId = m.id
WHERE e.salary > m.salary;
```

variables: N: total rows in Employee table
complexity.notes: Equi-join on primary key index with salary predicate filter.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated scalar subqueries inside a SELECT or WHERE clause execute once per row, resulting in O(N^2) evaluation without index caching.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: An inner self-join on indexed id requires O(N) time with O(1) extra space or O(N) hash join memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear aliasing of worker versus supervisor tables; recognizing inner join excludes employees without managers.
